I1.quote: The isothermal volumetric measurements were carried out by Hy-Energy’s PCTPro 2000 sorption equipment. This fully automated Sievert’s-type instrument uses an internal PID controlled pressure regulator with maximum pressure of 170 bar.

I2.quote: Searched for a measured sorbent with majority carbon by mass. Samples are PANI-STD, PANI-SnO2, PANI-Al and PANI with 10 wt% MWCNT: all polyaniline-matrix polymer composites, none carbonized; no neat carbon sample measured.

I3.quote: At 50 °C, however, the sample can store approximately 0.075 wt% hydrogen at 60 bar.
I3.location: main, p. 5 (journal p. 1014), Section 3, text below Fig. 7 (also Fig. 4 axes: pressure in bar, curves labelled by temperature)

I4.quote: Searched text and page images (Figs. 1-7) for surface area, BET, Langmuir, m2/g, N2 adsorption. Found none; characterization is FTIR, DSC, TGA and SEM, and porosity is only qualitative.

I5.quote: Nanomaterials have diverse tunable physical properties as a function of their size and shape due to strong quantum confinement effect and large surface to volume ratio.

notes: I2 is a judgment call on the 10 wt% MWCNT/polyaniline composite (Sections 2.1 and 3, journal pp. 1011-1012; Fig. 6, journal p. 1014): the majority component by mass is polyaniline, and sec. 3 excludes uncarbonized polymers, so it is not a carbon sorbent. The paper would also fail I4 (no surface area anywhere), so it is ineligible whichever way I2 is read; not_carbon is first in the section 4 order. I1, I3 and I5 are met. Not retracted (record is_retracted false, no retraction notice in the PDF), a primary article, and no statement that its uptake values were published before (ref. 10 is cited only as previous work).
